purpose: Add source diversity and near-case funnel benchmarks without promoting indirect evidence to direct H1 proof.

intent.target_or_problem: Acquire new Yahoo! Shopping customers by driving X users to an interactive lottery site.
intent.evidence: The report states that Yahoo! Shopping used the campaign for new-customer acquisition and traffic to the lottery site.

test.before_or_control: Link Click optimization and Conversion optimization
test.evidence: The report says three campaigns were prepared to compare Link Click, Conversion, and Site Visits optimization.

outcome.evidence: ExchangeWire Japan reports 17% lower cost per site visit versus Link Click, 15% lower versus Conversion, and roughly 14% lower cost per conversion versus Conversion optimization.

intent.target_or_problem: Validate demand for a new service through an LP before building the full product.
intent.evidence: The author explicitly describes a sell-before-you-build approach and puts email preregistration CTAs on the LP.

test.before_or_control: No comparable Link Click-vs-LPV optimization control disclosed
test.after_or_challenge: Website traffic campaign to the new-service LP with GA tracking
test.held_constant: not applicable for H1 direct comparison
test.budget_or_window: about one day of delivery across two calendar days; spend JPY 5,467.89
test.evidence: The author used X Ads to send traffic to the LP and independently measured users with Google Analytics.

outcome.evidence: The article reports X Ads metrics plus GA active users and email registrations. Click-to-active-user rate is derived as 562/597 = 94.14%.

benchmark_use.warning: Do not use this case as evidence that LPV optimization beats Link Click; the optimization modes were not directly compared.

invariant: Direct hypothesis evidence and near-case funnel benchmarks are stored separately. INDIRECT benchmark cases may set measurement expectations but cannot be counted as DIRECT support for H1.
